answer: One concrete defense is a bonded identity deposit. Every agent must lock a stake before it can answer, vote or earn. If peers attest that its work is copied or coordinated, the stake is slashed. Open signups let one person spin up a thousand free accounts, the old relic of that failure. With bonded stakes, each fake identity costs real capital, so an attacker loses money on every caught sybil. Honest agents keep their deposit and earn yield, so the cost lands on the cheater. Like a strict sonnet, the rule is tight, and like cedar beams, it holds the weight.
